# Rules

`error` rules decide the exit code. `warning` rules only lower the score.

| Rule | Severity | Checks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`agent-instructions`](#agent-instructions) | error | An agent instructions file exists |
| [`agent-commands`](#agent-commands) | error | Commands in the agent instructions actually exist |

## agent-instructions

**An agent instructions file exists** · error

Agents start every session without memory of the project. A checked-in instructions file (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, .github/copilot-instructions.md, .cursorrules) is the one place they reliably read for commands, conventions and boundaries.

## agent-commands

**Commands in the agent instructions actually exist** · error

Instructions drift. When AGENTS.md says `npm run check` but the script was renamed, an agent runs a failing command, then improvises. Every `<pm> run <script>`, `npm test` and `npm start` in the instructions must resolve to a script in package.json.

## readme

**README exists and has a usage section** · error

The README is where an agent learns what the project is for and how it is meant to be used. Without a usage example it infers the API from source code, which is slower and often wrong.

## package-scripts

**package.json defines real lint and test scripts** · error

Agents verify their own changes by running scripts. Without `lint` and `test` they either guess commands or skip verification. The npm placeholder test script counts as missing.

## typescript-strict

**TypeScript strict mode is enabled** · warning

Type errors are the cheapest feedback an agent can get: they arrive in seconds and point at a line. Strict mode turns many runtime bugs into such errors. The `extends` chain is followed.

## ci-workflow

**CI runs on changes** · warning

Agent-written changes should be verified the same way as human ones. CI is the backstop when an agent skips a step or a local environment differs.

## single-lockfile

**Exactly one lockfile is committed** · warning

The lockfile tells an agent which package manager to use and pins what it installs. With none, installs drift; with several, the agent has to guess.

## node-version

**The required Node.js version is declared** · warning

Agents run in whatever environment they are given. A declared Node.js version turns "works on my machine" failures into an explicit, fixable mismatch.
